content: Adverse reactions to terbinafine, as observed in clinical trials and postmarketing reports, include a range of effects across various organ systems. Below is a detailed description of these reactions: 1. Gastrointestinal Symptoms: Patients have reported diarrhea, dyspepsia (indigestion), and abdominal pain during clinical trials. These symptoms were generally mild and transient. 2. Liver Function Abnormalities: Abnormalities in liver function tests have been observed. In postmarketing reports, cases of liver failure, some requiring liver transplantation or resulting in death, have been documented. Other hepatic issues include idiosyncratic and symptomatic liver injury, hepatitis, cholestasis, and elevated liver enzymes. 3. Skin Reactions: Rashes, urticaria (hives), pruritus (itching), and photosensitivity reactions have been reported. Serious skin conditions such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, psoriasiform eruptions, exacerbation of psoriasis, and hair loss have also been noted. 4. Taste and Smell Disturbances: Taste disturbances, including complete loss of taste, have been reported. These disturbances can lead to reduced food intake, weight loss, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. Smell disturbances, including loss of smell, have also been observed. 5. Eye Disorders: Changes in the ocular lens and retina were noted during clinical trials, though their clinical significance remains unclear. Postmarketing reports include visual field defects and reduced visual acuity. 6. Hearing and Balance Issues: Hearing impairment, tinnitus (ringing in the ears), and vertigo (a sensation of spinning) have been reported. 7. Blood and Lymphatic System Disorders: Serious conditions such as pancytopenia (a reduction in all blood cell types), agranulocytosis (a severe reduction in white blood cells), severe neutropenia, thrombocytopenia (low platelet count), and anemia have been identified. 8. Immune System Disorders: Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including angioedema (swelling beneath the skin), anaphylaxis, and serum sickness-like reactions, have been reported. There have also been cases of cutaneous and systemic lupus erythematosus being precipitated or exacerbated. 9. Psychiatric Symptoms: Anxiety and depressive symptoms, independent of taste disturbances, have been reported. In some cases, depressive symptoms resolved after discontinuing terbinafine and recurred upon restarting the medication. 10. Nervous System Disorders: Cases of paresthesia (tingling or prickling sensations) and hypoesthesia (reduced sense of touch or sensation) have been reported. 11. Vascular Disorders: Vasculitis (inflammation of blood vessels) has been observed. 12. Gastrointestinal Disorders: Pancreatitis and vomiting have been reported. 13. Musculoskeletal Disorders: Rhabdomyolysis (a serious condition involving muscle breakdown), arthralgia (joint pain), and myalgia (muscle pain) have been noted. 14. General Symptoms: Malaise (a general feeling of discomfort), fatigue, influenza-like illness, and fever have been reported. 15. Investigations: Altered prothrombin time (both prolongation and reduction) has been observed in patients taking warfarin concurrently. Increased blood creatine phosphokinase levels have also been reported. In general, adverse reactions observed during clinical trials were mild and transient, rarely leading to discontinuation of the medication. However, postmarketing reports highlight the potential for serious and life-threatening reactions, underscoring the need for careful monitoring during terbinafine therapy.
